records.text: Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to inheritors,
and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.
Save me, Lord, for the holy one is gone; for truths have become few among the sons of men.
Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart.
May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and a boastful tongue—
those who said, “We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is our lord?”
Listen to Me, you who know judgment, My people with My law in your heart. Do not fear people’s reproach or be overcome by their contempt.
For a garment will be consumed by time, and wool eaten by a moth. But My righteousness will last for ever, and My salvation through generations of generations.”
Each of you, guard against his neighbor, and do not put trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.
Each will mock his friend; they certainly will not speak truth. Their tongue has learned to speak false things; they did wrong and did not cease turning back.
Interest upon interest, deceit upon deceit: they were unwilling to know Me.
Do not suppose that I came to bring peace upon the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
For I came to divide a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
and a person’s enemies will be the members of his own household.
I waited patiently for the Lord; He attended to me and heard my supplication.
He brought me up from a pit of misery and from muddy slime; He set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps.
He put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God. Many will see and fear and hope in the Lord.
for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.
He will give his cheek to the one striking him; he will be filled with reproaches.
For the Lord will not reject for ever.
For the One who humbled will have compassion according to His abundant mercy.
For He did not answer from His heart, and He humbled human beings.
To humble under one’s feet all the prisoners of the earth,
to turn aside a man’s judgment before the face of the Most High,
to condemn a person when he is judged—the Lord did not say to do this.
Who spoke in this way and it came to be? The Lord did not command,
will not calamities and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should a living person grumble, a man concerning his sin?
Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.
Let us lift our hearts upon our hands to the Exalted One in heaven.
We have sinned and acted godlessly, and Thou wast not propitiated.
My soul thirsted for the living God. When will I come and appear before God’s face?
My tears became my bread day and night, while it is said to me every day, “Where is your God?”
These things I remembered and poured out my soul within me: for I will pass through the place of a wonderful tent to God’s house, with a voice of exultation and thanksgiving, a celebrating sound.
The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?
I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
A partridge called; it gathered what it did not bear. One makes his wealth without judgment; in the middle of his days they will abandon him, and at his last he will be foolish.
For the end; concerning those who will be changed. A testimony for Asaph; a psalm concerning the Assyrian.
Thou who shepherdest Israel, pay attention, Thou who guidest Joseph like sheep; Thou who sittest upon the cherubim, appear.
Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, rouse Thy dominion, and come to save us.
God, turn us back; make Thy face shine, and we shall be saved.
The Lord rescued Israel that day from the Egyptians’ hand, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel saw the great hand in what the Lord had done to the Egyptians. The people feared the Lord and trusted God and His attendant Moses.
Behold, My servant will understand, and will be exalted and greatly glorified.
As many will be astonished at you— so your form will be without honour among men, and your glory among men—
so many nations will marvel at him, and kings will close their mouths. For those to whom he was not proclaimed will see, and those who have not heard will understand.

And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, cursed are you above all cattle and all the wild beasts of the earth. Upon your breast and belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel.
And he will rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.
Ethiopians will fall before him, and his enemies will lick dust.
kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.
And all kings will bow before him; all nations will serve him.
Who is like Thee among the gods, O Lord? Who is like Thee, glorified among the holy ones, marvellous in glories, working wonders?
Thou didst stretch forth Thy right hand; the earth swallowed them.
In Thy righteousness Thou didst guide this people of Thine whom Thou didst redeem; in Thy strength Thou didst comfort them to Thy holy dwelling.
The nations heard and were angry; pangs took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the leaders of Edom hastened; and trembling seized the rulers of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
May fear and trembling fall upon them; by the greatness of Thine arm let them become as stone, until Thy people pass over, O Lord, until this people of Thine whom Thou hast purchased pass over.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
He will not be angry to the end, nor maintain wrath for ever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,
for according to heaven’s height above the earth, the Lord strengthened His mercy toward those who fear Him.
As far as the east is distant from the west, He removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on children, the Lord had compassion on those who fear Him,
And an angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time out of the heaven,
saying, “By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and have not spared your beloved son for My sake,
surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.
And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have listened to My voice.”
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and accomplished redemption for His people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant,
as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from long ago:
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant,
the oath He swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, rescued from our enemies’ hand, we might serve Him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
And if the Lord your God destroys from before you the nations whither you go to inherit their land, and you inherit their possession and dwell in their land,

take heed unto yourself, that you do not seek to follow them after they have been destroyed from before you. You shall not inquire after their gods, saying: How do these nations serve their gods? I also will do so.
You shall not do so unto the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did unto their gods, for they burn their sons and their daughters with fire unto their gods.
